info.title: Open mSupply GraphQL API
info.description: Open mSupply is the mSupply Foundation's open-source Logistics Management Information System (LMIS) for public health supply chains. Its server exposes a single GraphQL endpoint at POST {baseUrl}/graphql taking a JSON body of the form `{query, variables}` and returning `{data, errors}`. This document is a mechanical conversion of the server's GraphQL schema (introspection): every root field of `Queries` and `Mutations` is one operation and every named GraphQL type is one component schema. Because OpenAPI 3.0 permits only one operation per method per path, each root field is modelled as a distinct `/graphql#<field>` path variant; at runtime all of them are the same POST to /graphql. The OpenFn msupply adaptor (@openfn/language-msupply) authenticates with the `authToken` query and then issues `items`, `insertOutboundShipment` and `batchOutboundShipment`, plus a generic `query()` operation that can send any document.

servers.description: Open mSupply demo server. Deployments are self-hosted; the adaptor's `baseUrl` credential sets the real host. The GraphQL endpoint is {baseUrl}/graphql.

post.description: The single Open mSupply GraphQL endpoint. Every other operation in this document is the same POST with a different document in `query`; the `/graphql#<field>` path variants exist only so each root field can carry its own operationId and response schema. This is the adaptor's generic `query(query, variables)` operation.

post.description: GraphQL query `itemsByStockLineFilter`(storeId, page, filter, sort). Send it as `{ query, variables }` to POST {baseUrl}/graphql; the selection set determines which fields of the payload come back. Query for items that have at least one stock_line matching `filter` in `store_id`, sorted/paginated by item attributes. Companion to `stockLines`: same filter shape, but the result is one row per item (suitable for an aggregated/grouped stock view). Because the predicate is identical to what `stockLines` uses, an item appears here iff at least one of its stock lines would appear in `stockLines`.
